paper_title: Improved bounds on ultralight scalar dark matter in the radio-frequency range
notes: Paper constrains both g_e (electron mass coupling) and g_γ (fine-structure constant coupling) via fundamental constant oscillations in the 20 kHz–100 MHz range. The primary results are presented in Fig. 2 as exclusion plots. Data points extracted from Fig. 2(a) for the galactic halo scenario (ρ_DM ≈ 3×10^-6 eV^4). The paper uses d_me = g_e M_Pl / m_e,0 (dimensionless form shown in Fig. 3). Experiment B provides the main constraints (Apparatus A is noted as requiring further design improvements). The coupling_type is ScalarElectron because the paper's primary observable is oscillations in the electron mass m_e via the coupling g_e. The dm_density_assumed (3×10^-6 eV^4) is the standard galactic halo value used throughout. Extraction confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (1) the paper presents results in graphical form (Fig. 2) rather than tabular data, requiring visual extraction; (2) multiple coupling scenarios are discussed (galactic, solar, and Earth halos), and we report the galactic case; (3) the paper also constrains g_γ (photon coupling), but the pre-analysis hint and the emphasis on electron mass variation in Fig. 3 support ScalarElectron as the primary coupling type. The data points are approximate readings from Fig. 2(a) top panel and should be cross-checked against the paper's supplementary materials if available. | selector: text (sole candidate)
